sources.title: Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation
sources.text:
# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

sources.title: Utilities area and service directory
sources.text:
# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

sources.title: Record and measurement conventions
sources.text:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

sources.title: Change and work-record requirements
sources.text:
# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Utilities point register extract

Record ID: IA-P02 | Configuration revision: PR-12 | Effective: 2024-05-01

| Point | Location/input | Description and scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P-U | Site header H-U, north gallery | Pressure upstream of the 1SC distribution routes |
| P-R | RHOB receiving header H-R | Pressure at the RHOB instrument-air receiving station |
| C-11 RUN | C-11 starter auxiliary contact | Common-header compressor motor running indication; not a local flow proof |
| AL-44 | RHOB PLC low-pressure input from P-R | Active below 4.5 bar; clears above 5.0 bar |

AL-44 display text was retained as “COMP FAULT” from an earlier operator-screen template. PR-12 maps it to the receiving-header pressure condition, not to C-11's trip contact.

This register maps signals. It does not establish the state of any distribution valve or prove that every supply disturbance would appear in the selected sample export.

sources.title: Initial desk message
sources.text:
# Initial desk message

Record ID: IA-C01 | Entered: 2024-05-20 10:04 | Channel: copied radio/desk note

The note is an unverified contemporaneous account.

“RHOB called air trouble. COMP FAULT on screen, acknowledged around 10:03. Might have lost the compressor again; similar call last winter. Utilities checking.”

Recorder: desk relief operator D-R. Basis recorded: screen label and radio call. The recorder was not at C-11 and did not inspect its starter or observe a trip. The note's 10:03 time is the acknowledgment time as recalled by the recorder. No compressor trip log is attached.

sources.title: Installation completion and line-register extract
sources.text:
# Installation completion and line-register extract

Record ID: IA-P04 | Change: CH-218 | Mechanical completion: 2024-05-16

## Completion entry

East service-rack line addition completed under CH-218. Installed line identification: B-17. Field redline retained as DW-1SC-17 revision B-RL. Redline status: field record; operating-document issue status not stated on this sheet. Scope of signature: installed items and labeling only.

## Connection schedule

Each row identifies one physical segment. Rows describe connectivity, not valve position or permitted use.

| Segment | From | Through/component | To |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N-01 | H-U site header | M-101 | D-101 inlet |
| N-02 | D-101 outlet | M-102 | H-R receiving header |
| B-17a | H-U site header | V-201 | B-17 spool |
| B-17b | B-17 spool | V-202 | H-R receiving header |

V-201 and V-202 are inline valves at opposite ends of B-17. There is no intervening feed into the B-17 spool in this register. N-01/N-02 form the normal dryer route. B-17 is the auxiliary route associated with the maintenance service arrangement.

The installation record includes no incident-day operating positions, no work-boundary acceptance and no approval of the issued ECP revision.

sources.title: WO-527 field execution and observation log
sources.text:
# WO-527 field execution and observation log

Record ID: IA-P05 | Compiled: 2024-05-20 16:00

No original photographs are supplied.

## Field worksheet and incident observations

| Time | Source | Recorded observation/action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approximately 09:56 | U-A worksheet | V-201 moved to open position during preparation. |
| 10:00:03, within 5 seconds | Gallery clock/video review transcript | U-A completes closure of M-101; U-B present. No contact with V-202 is visible in this camera's coverage. |
| 10:02 | Work-folder hold entry | Preparation stopped. No maintenance opening of pipework or dryer covers commenced. |
| 10:05:40, within 5 seconds | U-B field note and photograph-description transcript | V-202 handle across line at east rack; identified against its fixed tag. Recorded as closed. M-102 recorded open. |
| 10:06:18, within 5 seconds | U-B action note | V-202 moved to open position. M-101 left closed; M-102 left open. |
| Approximately 10:07 | RHOB radio entry | Local air indication back in normal band. |

The field photo description is a text surrogate, not an image that has been independently inspected. A handle-position observation alone does not establish internal condition.

## Interview scope

U-A and U-B confirmed that the folder received was the one indexed in IA-S02. They recalled identifying V-201 during preparation. Neither interview supplies a reason that V-202 remained closed. Neither interview states that a two-valve instruction was read and deliberately ignored.

The main-route isolation remained incomplete when the service interruption occurred. The work was held at preparation and then deferred. These records do not establish exposure of a maintenance worker to an energized open system.

sources.title: Distribution inspection and follow-up notes
sources.text:
# Distribution inspection and follow-up notes

Record ID: IA-P06 | Inspection: 2024-05-20 10:20–11:10

Inspectors used the tags H-U, M-101, D-101, M-102, V-201, V-202 and H-R. The installed B-17 line joined the points shown on the CH-218 connection schedule. Both V-201 and V-202 were present; a label was legible at each location.

No pipe rupture, separated fitting or obvious sustained air discharge was observed along the inspected gallery-to-RHOB route. This was a post-restoration walkdown, not a full leak-rate test or a measurement of incident-time demand.

No C-11 repair or reset was performed between the initial call and recovery. The pressure recovery occurred before this inspection began. The inspection did not test all possible transient compressor faults or quantify every receiving load.

Photograph descriptions taken after 10:20 show V-201 and V-202 open. These later positions do not establish their positions before the interruption. IA-P05 is the retained pre-restoration observation record.

## Workflow definition retained with export

For this form version, an answer of “Yes” in the maintenance-boundary-impact field creates an ECP/distribution review task. “No” routes to installation completion without that task. Completion of that route does not independently validate the selected impact value.

This export includes the routing history and all generated task IDs. No ECP/distribution task was generated under CH-218. It does not include the preparer's reasoning for the “No” selection, informal conversations, management direction or a finding about intent.

## Draft revision 4-D scope index

The draft adds B-17, V-201, V-202 and the RHOB receiving-point service check to the work-document scope. Its approval field remained unsigned at the time of WO-527 issue. Its author recorded “awaiting change disposition.” This draft is evidence of proposed content, not proof that it was communicated or authorized for execution.

## Retrieval scope

The records custodian checked the issued-document register, WO-527 retained attachments and temporary-instruction register for this job/date. No issued temporary instruction covering B-17 was found. This does not prove that no informal discussion occurred. The confirmed supplied document set remained the one in IA-S02.

sources.title: Journal reconciliation and supplementary interview
sources.text:
# Journal reconciliation and supplementary interview

Record ID: IA-P09 | Compiled: 2024-05-21 11:00

## Time and event checks

The full C-11 starter event journal for 09:50–10:15 contains no stop, trip, restart or reset event. The journal's event-capture diagnostic reports no gap within that window. This narrows the recorded trip explanation; it is not a test of all possible compressor performance defects.

The historian, RHOB alarm journal and gallery clock were checked against the same site time reference. Their recorded clock offsets were within five seconds. Field times in IA-P05 retain their stated uncertainty. The journal's AL-44 occurrence time is 10:00:32; 10:03:14 is acknowledgment, not onset.

## Supplementary statement from desk recorder D-R

“I wrote compressor because that was the screen wording. I did not see a trip at C-11. The 10:03 time I wrote was when the alarm was acknowledged. I had no field report identifying a compressor failure.”

The original IA-C01 entry remains in the file. This statement clarifies its basis; it does not erase the fact that an air-low event occurred.

No evidence collected in this record identifies deliberate noncompliance, a monetary motive, deficient staffing or the reason for the change-form classification.
